title: Automated config safety net for batching & caching: staged apply, anomaly detectors, and state reconciliation
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Summary: Implement an automated safety net around configuration changes that touch batching and caching heuristics. The goal is to enable confident automated recommendations (from Optimize) and operator-initiated config applies while guaranteeing quick, observable, and reversible behavior when changes cause regressions. This ticket covers: 1) change staging model (canary/shadow/dry-run), 2) anomaly detectors and rollback triggers, 3) guardrails (hard limits and sanity checks), and 4) periodic state reconciliation to detect and repair drift between desired config and applied runtime state. Motivation: recent experiments with adaptive batching and prefix-KV TTL tweaks reduced unit cost but produced transient latency regressions in tail p95 for some tenants. We need an end-to-end safe apply/rollback system so recommendations can be applied automatically or via fast-track with low operational risk. Design decisions and trade-offs: - Two-phase rollout: shadow applies (no traffic) -> lightweight canary (1–5% traffic) -> progressive rollout with automatic stop/rollback. This balances fast iteration with safety. - Metrics-based triggers rather than single-check heuristics: monitor latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token-per-second throughput, and cost-per-token proxy. Use statistical test (CUSUM + nonparametric bootstrapped delta) to detect regressions with configurable sensitivity per-customer. - Rollback windows: automatic immediate rollback for SLO violations above aggressive thresholds (e.g., p95 increase > 20% absolute or error rate increase > 1% absolute), soft stop/hold for marginal signals (5–20% p95 increase) and require manual review. Thresholds are configurable per environment. - Guardrails: enforce global hard limits (max_batch_size, max_concurrent_sequences, min_kv_cache_ttl, min_prefix_cache_hits) and model-specific safe profiles (never enable certain quantization modes in canary for affected models). - Safe apply mechanics: all config changes are applied via the control plane with a pre-check step that runs a dry-run simulation against a synthetic workload representative of the customer's recent traffic profile. If dry-run fails basic sanity checks, abort early. - State reconciliation: runtime agents periodically report effective config snapshots with versioned hashes. The reconcile controller compares desired state to reported state, detects drift, and attempts automated repair with exponential backoff. Persistent mismatches create an incident ticket and open a sticky rollback if necessary. - Observability & audit: every apply/rollback is logged with operator, reason, metrics at time of action, and linked PR/Recommendation. Console should show per-change timeline and an option to 'replay' the decision (re-run metric comparison). - Integration with Optimize recommendations: recommendations include a risk score and recommended rollout plan. The safety net consumes the risk score to pick default thresholds and can override to a more conservative plan for high-risk customers. Implementation plan (phases): Phase 1 (MVP, 3 sprints): - Build change staging engine in control plane (shadow/canary flags, traffic routing hooks). - Implement baseline anomaly detector + simple thresholds for p95 and error rate. - Add pre-apply dry-run simulation harness using recent traffic traces. - Add logging and basic Console timeline. Phase 2 (2 sprints): - Add statistical tests (CUSUM/bootstrapping) and adaptive sensitivity tuning. - Implement state reconciliation controller with exponential backoff and incidenting. - Wire in Optimize risk score and default rollout heuristics. Phase 3 (1–2 sprints): - Add model-specific guardrail profiles, additional metrics (token cost), and richer Console controls (rollback reasons, manual freeze). - Run cross-customer canaries and runbook for on-call escalation. Testing and validation: - Integration test harness that replays recorded tenant traffic against a canary binary and asserts metric delta behavior. - Chaos tests: inject artificial latency or error increases during rollout to validate rollback path. - Load tests on Dedicated pools to validate reconcile controller scale (10k agents). Security & compliance: - All change metadata and snapshots are encrypted at rest and access-logged. - Audit trail must be exportable for compliance reviews. - security_review_required: true (see metadata). Open questions / trade-offs: - How conservative should default thresholds be vs. letting Optimize pick aggressive, cost-saving configs? Proposal: default conservative for enterprise customers, opt-in aggressive for PLG. - Should the reconcile controller be allowed to auto-rollback stale changes without human approval? Proposal: allow auto-rollback only when SLOs are violated above 'auto' thresholds; otherwise create incident. - How to surface partial failures when only a subset of runtime agents fail to apply? We will treat >10% divergence in cluster as soft-fail and hold rollout until convergence. Links: design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Config+Safety+Net , PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4589 , demo dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/safety-net-demo
acceptance_criteria: Control plane can perform shadow and 1% canary applies and roll back automatically based on defined triggers
Dry-run simulation blocks at least 90% of obviously unsafe config changes (by synthetic workload)
State reconciliation detects drift within 2 minutes and attempts automated repair with exponential backoff
Console shows per-change timeline with metrics before and after and a one-click rollback
Integration tests and chaos tests pass in CI (no regression to existing rollout traffic path)
